To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the managers’ research priority topics were most frequently related to land-use planning decisions (in forests); (ii) the managers’ priority topics were less related to political decisions; and (iii) the managers’ views tended to focus on short term effects of conservation.

the managers’ research gap prioritization can be effectively implemented as a rapid, transparent, and low-cost procedure, which is suitable for the national scale and can be easily repeated in other countries.

(i) managers in Estonia consider land use planning decisions as most lacking critical knowledge, while political decision-making was considered as less lacking critical knowledge; (ii) the priority topics proposed for conservation management focused on management techniques for wetlands and forests, whereas the priority topics proposed to political decision makers focused on agricultural policy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the practical application of conservation science and the communication between scientists and the managers, and it is hoped that the procedure and results may be useful for other countries.
the practical application of the concept of research priority-setting, rather than with its theoretical aspects.
the knowledge problems of conservation managers and policy makers, and it is hoped that it can be useful to researchers who wish to contribute to conservation management and policy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the managers’ perspective on the research gaps in conservation management and policymaking is important to understand, and that it can be obtained through a rapid and transparent procedure.

, in Estonia, the most important knowledge gaps for national conservation are in the field of land-use planning, particularly in forestry, and the management techniques of artificial wetland drainage.
the procedure was useful, but not sufficient, to bridge the gap between conservation research and management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
managers and researchers should work together to identify the most critical research topics in order to make conservation management more effective.
managers’ views are important to consider in the research agenda of the scientists.
the procedure was useful for the managers and the researchers, but the researchers should not expect the managers to have a long-term view of conservation problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the managers’ views on the knowledge needs in conservation are not necessarily in conflict with the researchers’ views on the most important research topics.
, for the managers, the research topics are not necessarily the most important ones, but the most urgent ones.
the knowledge gap prioritization is a feasible procedure to facilitate communication between managers and scientists and to focus the research on the most urgent conservation issues.
